fixed: Typing or pasting a poussette, zig-zag, figure 8 or box circulate the way the figure list shows it now gives that figure, with its dancers, fraction, direction, ender and who leads. So does a swing with the way it ends facing, a promenade on a diagonal or facing a way, a single file circle, a facing star counterclockwise, and a revolving door, give and take, down the hall or up the hall that names third corners, opposites or a single neighbor, partner or shadow; "forward then backward" in a hall figure is read too. "Bend the line" at the end of a hall figure is still kept as a note. In Leads/Follows wording, most of these figures are not read yet when they name the leads or the follows. A poussette imported from ContraDB now turns the way ContraDB says: "back then left" is clockwise. The import read it the other way round before, so a ContraDB poussette you imported earlier may show the opposite turn; importing that dance again corrects it. Searching ContraDB for a poussette's direction now finds the direction you chose.

The ContraDB figure reader reads the app's display wording for a poussette, zig-zag and figure 8 (`_poussetteDisplay`, `_zigZagDisplay`, `_figure8Display`) and the display's subjects and `others` in a box circulate's cross-while-loop clause. It also reads a swing's displayed ending facing (`_swingEndFacingDisplay`, a whole line only), a promenade's displayed direction (in both the ContraDB and shared readers), a `single file circle`, a counterclockwise facing star, the display's subjects in a revolving door, give and take, facing star and the halls, and a hall's "forward then backward". ContraDB's own poussette reader now maps "back then left" to clockwise, as libfigure writes it (the poussette's turn is its `spin` parameter, whose clock wording writes `true` as "clockwise", and `poussetteWords` writes `true` as "back then left"); it read the sides reversed, and the ContraDB search translation's poussette mapping, inverted to match it, is un-inverted. Not read on purpose: a hall's "bend the line" ender, which ContraDB's own tests keep as a note; a figure 8 with no direction (`where: none`) and a box circulate without its balance, whose ContraDB and beat-implied readings this would override. The display's singular subjects in a take are read only on a whole line, and a figure 8 display line only with its own between pair and a single-dancer lead, so an import's custom lines are not newly force-matched. A trailing display direction is now read only where it ends the clause, so `facing up the hall` after a pass through, chain, pull by or right left through stays a note. Leads/Follows lines naming a role in a poussette, revolving door, box circulate, zig-zag, facing star or figure 8 still do not read back: free-text entry reads a line as typed before it applies the dialect's role words, and the as-typed reading already finds the move with the rest kept as a note.
